register.summary: Adds a path under `/<app>`: words typed as they are and `<name>` arguments, separated by spaces.
params: called with the typed arguments in the order of the path, passed as a value
optional: a list passed after the typed arguments, the same on every call
register.returns: `true`. What `function` returns becomes the result of the command: a number as it is, anything else `1` if true and `0` if false.
register.note: The number of parameters of the function is checked against the path when `register` runs, not when someone types the command. Nothing is printed on its own: answer the player with `print` or `core.mc.text`.

argument.summary: Declares the type of the arguments called `<name>`.
params: the name used between `<` and `>` in the paths
a map with a `'type'`, one of `command.types()`, and the modifiers of that type
argument.note: An undeclared name gets its type from the name itself, as in Scarpet: `<from_pos>` is a `pos`, `<count_int>` an `int`, anything else a `string`. A type or modifier that does not exist stops the load, with the right name suggested.

permission.summary: Who can use the command of the app.
params: `'all'` (the default), `'ops'`, a level `1`…`4`, `'players'`, `'server'`, or a function `fn(player) -> bool`
permission.note: The game decides who sees the command when they join: a function that changes its answer over time may show it to someone who cannot use it, but typing it is always checked again.

allow_conflicts.summary: Lets through two paths that take different arguments at the same point, which are otherwise a load error.
allow_conflicts.note: Brigadier accepts such paths and then suggests badly, which looks like a command that works: that is why they are refused by default.

list.summary: The paths the app has declared so far, as they are typed.

types.summary: The names of the built-in argument types.
